# Comprehensive Learning Guide: Recommendation Systems Theory and Coding in JS

## Course Overview

This hard-difficulty course bridges the gap between algorithmic foundations and real-world recommendation engine implementation using JavaScript. Recommendation systems are at the core of major tech companies (Netflix, Amazon, Spotify, YouTube), making this knowledge invaluable for both coding interviews and system design rounds.

**Who it's for:**
- Intermediate to advanced JavaScript developers preparing for FAANG or fintech interviews
- Backend engineers building personalization features
- Data-focused engineers transitioning to ML-adjacent roles
- Candidates targeting roles in recommendation platforms or e-commerce

**Why it matters:**
- Tests deep understanding of algorithms, data structures, and linear algebra
- Demonstrates ability to balance complexity with performance constraints
- Shows maturity in handling real constraints: sparsity, scalability, cold-start problems
- Common in take-home assignments and senior engineer rounds
- Bridges software engineering and machine learning domains

---

## Core Topics Covered

- **Collaborative Filtering** — Memory-based and model-based approaches; user-user and item-item similarity
- **Content-Based Filtering** — Feature extraction, similarity metrics, and hybrid methods
- **Matrix Factorization & SVD** — Dimensionality reduction, latent factors, and efficient computation
- **Similarity Metrics** — Cosine similarity, Euclidean distance, Pearson correlation, Jaccard index
- **Evaluation Metrics** — Precision@K, Recall@K, NDCG, MAP, and A/B testing frameworks
- **Scalability & Optimization** — Caching strategies, incremental updates, approximate nearest neighbors (ANN)
- **Cold-Start & Exploration Problems** — Handling new users/items, bandit algorithms, diversity
- **Real-World Implementations** — Handling sparse data, implicit feedback, temporal dynamics, and ranking

---

## Learning Path Workflow

### Phase 1: Foundations (Tasks 1–12)
**Goals:** Build intuition about recommendation problems; master similarity metrics

1. **Task 1–2:** Core concept: What is a recommendation system? Build a naive nearest-neighbor recommender
2. **Task 3–5:** Implement Cosine Similarity from scratch (with and without normalization)
3. **Task 6–7:** Euclidean Distance and Manhattan Distance implementations
4. **Task 8–9:** Pearson Correlation and handling edge cases (zero variance, sparse data)
5. **Task 10–11:** Jaccard Similarity for implicit/set-based feedback
6. **Task 12:** Benchmark similarity metrics on synthetic datasets

**Checkpoint:** Write a utility library with all 5 similarity metrics; unit test edge cases

---

### Phase 2: User-Based Collaborative Filtering (Tasks 13–25)
**Goals:** Implement classic collaborative filtering; understand memory complexity

7. **Task 13–15:** Build a user-user similarity matrix; handle sparsity
8. **Task 16–18:** Implement user-based k-NN recommendations with weighted aggregation
9. **Task 19–20:** Add bias correction (user mean ratings, global mean)
10. **Task 21–22:** Implement top-K selection with efficient partial sorting
11. **Task 23–24:** Handle cold-start users (new user problem); implement fallback strategies
12. **Task 25:** Optimize memory usage for large user populations

**Checkpoint:** Build a complete user-based CF system on MovieLens dataset; achieve reasonable precision@10

---

### Phase 3: Item-Based Collaborative Filtering (Tasks 26–35)
**Goals:** Compare user-based vs. item-based; optimize for real-time serving

13. **Task 26–28:** Build item-item similarity matrix; compare to user-based CF
14. **Task 29–31:** Implement item-based recommendations with efficient lookup tables
15. **Task 32–33:** Add temporal weighting (recent ratings matter more)
16. **Task 34–35:** Compare serving latency: user-based vs. item-based for online systems

**Checkpoint:** Implement both approaches; write performance comparison document

---

### Phase 4: Matrix Factorization & SVD (Tasks 36–48)
**Goals:** Move beyond neighborhood methods to latent factor models

17. **Task 36–38:** Implement Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) from scratch or via numeric library
18. **Task 39–41:** Build a Funk-SVD (SGD-based matrix factorization) model
19. **Task 42–44:** Handle implicit feedback with weighted matrix factorization
20. **Task 45–46:** Implement alternating least squares (ALS) for scalability
21. **Task 47–48:** Compare latent factor quality across different K values

**Checkpoint:** Train MF model on implicit feedback data; evaluate reconstruction error and recommendation quality

---

### Phase 5: Content-Based & Hybrid Systems (Tasks 49–58)
**Goals:** Leverage item metadata; combine multiple approaches

22. **Task 49–51:** Implement content-based filtering with TF-IDF feature vectors
23. **Task 52–53:** Build metadata similarity (tags, categories, genres)
24. **Task 54–56:** Create hybrid recommender (CF + content-based weighting)
25. **Task 57–58:** Implement diversity boosting and re-ranking strategies

**Checkpoint:** Build a hybrid system; measure diversity vs. accuracy tradeoff

---

### Phase 6: Evaluation & Ranking (Tasks 59–65)
**Goals:** Measure recommendation quality rigorously

26. **Task 59–60:** Implement Precision@K, Recall@K, F1@K metrics
27. **Task 61–62:** Build NDCG (Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain) evaluator
28. **Task 63–64:** Implement Mean Average Precision (MAP) and Hit Rate
29. **Task 65:** A/B testing framework and statistical significance testing

**Checkpoint:** Write a comprehensive evaluation suite; validate on benchmark datasets

---

### Phase 7: Advanced Topics & Scalability (Tasks 66–73)
**Goals:** Handle production constraints; implement advanced techniques

30. **Task 66–67:** Implement Locality-Sensitive Hashing (LSH) for approximate nearest neighbors
31. **Task 68–69:** Build incremental/online learning system (handle new ratings in real-time)
32. **Task 70:** Implement bandit-based exploration (epsilon-greedy, UCB)
33. **Task 71:** Add caching layer and cache invalidation strategy
34. **Task 72–73:** Full system design: integrate all components; benchmark end-to-end latency

**Checkpoint:** Build a complete, production-aware recommendation engine; document trade-offs

---

## Key Skills You'll Build

### Algorithmic Competencies
- **Similarity computation** at scale (optimized implementations, vectorization awareness)
- **Sparse matrix operations** (efficient storage, avoiding dense computations)
- **Graph algorithms** (understanding recommendation as a graph traversal problem)
- **Linear algebra** (SVD, eigenvalue decomposition, rank approximation)

### Engineering Patterns
- **Caching and memoization** (pre-compute expensive similarity matrices)
- **Lazy evaluation** (on-demand computation for serving)
- **Approximate algorithms** (trade accuracy for speed via LSH, sampling)
- **Incremental updates** (handling streaming data without full recomputation)

### System Design Intuition
- **Batch vs. online** trade-offs (pre-computing recommendations vs. real-time computation)
- **Cold-start handling** (fallback strategies, content-based bridging)
- **Diversity vs. accuracy** (avoiding filter bubbles, exploration-exploitation)
- **Performance profiling** (identifying bottlenecks in recommendation pipelines)

### JavaScript-Specific Skills
- **Working with typed arrays** (Float32Array for matrix storage)
- **Async/await for batch processing** (non-blocking recommendation computation)
- **Stream processing** (handling incremental data updates)
- **Performance optimization** (reducing GC pressure, efficient data structures)

---
